verdict: Microsoft grew 17% to $61.9B as Azure jumped 31% and Microsoft Cloud revenue hit $35.1B — and it kept $21.9B as profit, about 35 cents of every dollar.

segments.name: Productivity and Business Processes
segments.note: Office 365, LinkedIn and Dynamics — Office Commercial cloud services grew 13%, LinkedIn 10% and Dynamics 365 23%.

segments.name: Intelligent Cloud
segments.note: Azure and server products — Azure and other cloud services grew 31%, the fastest-growing large piece.

segments.name: More Personal Computing
segments.note: Windows, Xbox and search ads — Xbox content and services up 62% on the Activision acquisition, Windows up 11%, devices down 17%.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Spending on building products, led by AI and cloud — up 10% YoY.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling and marketing the product line — up 8% YoY.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day — up 16% YoY.

follow100Note: The rows reconcile to the $35.47 kept as profit within $0.01 of rounding; other expense is a $1.38 drag per $100 of revenue.
footerNote: Segments use Microsoft's FY24 reporting structure (three segments, as reported at the time).

takeaways.title: Azure accelerated
takeaways.text: Azure and other cloud services grew 31% — faster than the quarter before — as AI demand added to regular cloud growth; Microsoft Cloud overall reached $35.1B, up 23%.

takeaways.title: Growth was broad-based
takeaways.text: All three segments grew at double-digit rates — Intelligent Cloud +21%, More Personal Computing +17% (Xbox content +62% on the Activision deal) and Productivity and Business Processes +12%.

takeaways.title: A third of sales became profit
takeaways.text: Net income rose 20% to $21.9B — about 35 cents of every revenue dollar — even as Microsoft kept spending heavily on the data centers behind its AI push.
